score.notes: A disciplined, clearly intentional temple face with a legible base→middle→crown. The massing is symmetric and the bay logic is readable: a dark plinth, a mid-register framed by gold-capped pilasters (nice torch/flame motifs), a central arched portal with a chevron keystone device, and a crown that reads as a dentiled cornice carrying a colonnade of teal-infilled bays plus a projecting parapet. Color is the strongest card — a dominant near-black ground with gold as the structuring accent and teal as the supporting hue is a well-judged, Egyptian/Deco-flavored scheme that gives the building its identity without tipping into garish. Detail is genuinely rich through the upper two-thirds (pilaster capitals, the entablature band, the portal surround), which keeps it above competent. What holds every dimension at strong rather than exceptional: the lower corners and the plinth are large flat dark fields with no articulation, the parapet caps read slightly clumsy/stuck-on against the otherwise tight cornice, and the central doorway itself is a plain dark void with only a thin teal sill — the most important element is the least resolved. Each of those is an easy, nameable improvement, so none of the dimensions reach the apex. Reads unmistakably as a grand temple and would photograph well, but it is not yet a namable landmark.
